content_list.content_text: Canadians have to spend a lot of time patiently explaining that they are not American. Likewise, films made in Canada - with Toronto standing in for New York - are often hard to tell apart from those produced in the United States. This may be why certain Canadian directors make a point of creating works that set them apart from Hollywood's mainstream output.

information.contentText: After filming wrapped in early 1986, several excerpts of the footage were shown to Fox executives, who were very impressed. Fearing a negative audience reaction, a sequence featuring a hybrid "monkey-cat" animal was cut from the film to make it easier for the audience to sympathize with Brundle's character. Another advance test screening was later held on the Fox lot in Los Angeles, and this one featured a "butterfly baby"; as before, the results of that screening led to the scene being cut.

content_list.content_text: Even those whose careers have every so often taken them to the Los Angeles studios, such as David Cronenberg (b. 1943), resisted assimilation and continue to make unmistakably individual films, while the output of Canadian filmmakers such as Denys Arcand (b. 1941), Guy Maddin (b. 1956) and Atom Egoyan (b. 1960) remains proudly and determinedly idiosyncratic.

David Cronenberg started out making ultra-low-budget underground films, but carried his recurring theme of "body horror" (body horror) into the sensationalist mainstream in productions such as his breakthrough film Shivers (1975). In it, as in the surreal Videodrome (1983), the theme of parasites and other elements that can invade the human body and turn against it becomes a metaphor for psychological and social dissolution.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from The Decline of the American Empire
information.contentText: According to Télérama, "The film's daring lies in having bet everything on dialogue: first in echo (the men's side against the women's side), then crisscrossed (everyone together). At times, we are bothered by how easily it says something funny or shocking...".

content_list.content_text: During the 1980s, his budgets grew, and with them the technical and narrative sophistication of his films, leading to his masterful reworking of the "teleportation gone wrong" story, The Fly (1986) - a rare example of a remake that completely surpassed the original - and Dead Ringers (1988), featuring the best dual performance of Jeremy Irons's career as twin gynecologists with increasingly bizarre obsessions.

quote.quote: The Fly is that rare kind of film – a remake that clearly surpasses the original, and in every expectation.
quote.author: Boston Globe on The Fly (1986)

content_list.content_text: Atom Egoyan (b. 1960) likewise started small and moved progressively toward the mainstream. Drawing on his own Armenian-Canadian background and his family's turbulent history, he made a series of films in the 1980s – among them Peep Show (1981) and Family Viewing (1987) - that dealt insistently with problems of ethnic identity, dysfunctional homes, broken homes, alienation, loss and death. Alongside these themes lies an uneasy fascination with the role of visual media in the modern world. His characters obsessively use film and video to reconstruct reality so that it fits their desires - identity takes the form of a charade. Egoyan himself commented: "My films are designed to make viewers self-conscious. I take pride in that."

information.contentText: The basis for Videodrome came from David Cronenberg's childhood. Cronenberg used to pick up television signals from Buffalo, New York, late at night after the Canadian stations had gone off the air, and worried about seeing something disturbing not meant for public consumption. As Cronenberg explained, "I've always been interested in dark things and in other people's fascination with dark things. Also, the idea of people locking themselves in a room and turning the key on a television set so they can watch something extremely obscure, and in doing so, allowing themselves to explore their fascinations."

content_list.content_text: Unlike Cronenberg and Egoyan, Guy Maddin shows little interest in making films for the mainstream circuit. His debut feature, Tales from the Gimli Hospital (1988), was so strange it could almost be seen as an act of contempt, a retro pastiche of silent-film stylization, with minimal dialogue, full of incoherences that provoke the viewer with a crazy logic.

Quebec filmmakers are naturally distinguished from their American colleagues by language, while at the same time remaining distant from and different to their European cousins so as not to be absorbed into the French-language circuit. Denys Arcand, the best-known French-Canadian director on the international scene, started out making short documentaries for the National Film Board of Canada, but his radical political positions and independent nature created tension with his bosses.

information.contentText: The film was a success at the time, winning Best Feature Film at the Toronto International Film Festival.

content_list.content_text: His first three features, including Gina (1975), used the thriller to explore political themes, but his views aroused official suspicion, and for some years he was given few resources to work with. Arcand bounced back in grand style with Le déclin de l'empire américain (The Decline of the American Empire, 1986), which was nominated for an Oscar, as was his next film, Jésus de Montréal (Jesus of Montreal, 1989), an intensely ironic fable about an actor who plays Christ in the city's annual Passion play and discovers that the role is taking control of his life.

quote.quote: Despite the fact that Videodrome came and went faster than Superman and his bullet, it is still an excellent film. It is a high-caliber genre film that raises a number of important questions.
quote.author: Christopher John on Videodrome (1983)

content_list.content_text: The saddest decline in Canadian cinema was surely that of Claude Jutra (1930-1986). In 1971, he directed Mon oncle Antoine (1971), which received a shower of awards and was voted the best Canadian film of all time in 1984. But his subsequent work was disappointing. In the mid-1980s, he was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, and he died in 1986 after disappearing from his home. When the St. Lawrence River thawed in April 1987, his body was found in its waters.

movies.title: The Fly
movies.overview: When Seth Brundle makes a huge scientific and technological breakthrough in teleportation, he decides to test it on himself. Unbeknownst to him, a common housefly manages to get inside the device and the two become one.

movies.title: Videodrome
movies.overview: As the president of a trashy TV channel, Max Renn is desperate for new programming to attract viewers. When he happens upon "Videodrome," a TV show dedicated to gratuitous torture and punishment, Max sees a potential hit and broadcasts the show on his channel. However, after his girlfriend auditions for the show and never returns, Max investigates the truth behind Videodrome and discovers that the graphic violence may not be as fake as he thought.

movies.title: Family Viewing
movies.overview: An emotionally constrained view of the displacement of human feelings in our video saturated society. Van regularly visits his grandmother in a run-down nursing home. His father depends on phone sex for guidance meanwhile erasing family homevideos of happier times with homemade pornography. Will Van rescue his grandmother and memories of his mother in time?

movies.title: Jesus of Montreal
movies.overview: A group of actors putting on an interpretive Passion Play in Montreal begin to experience a meshing of their characters and their private lives as the production takes form against the growing opposition of the Catholic church.

movies.title: The Decline of the American Empire
movies.overview: Four very different Montreal university teachers gather at a rambling country house to prepare a dinner. Remy (married), Claude (a homosexual), Pierre (involved with a girlfriend) and Alain (a bachelor) discuss sex, the female body and their affairs with them. Meanwhile, their four female guests, Louise (Remy's wife of 15 years), Dominique (a spinster), Diane (a divorcée) and Danielle (Pierre's girlfriend) are spending the time at a downtown health gym. They also discuss sex, the female body and, naturally, men. Later in the evening, they finally meet at the country house and have dinner. A ninth guest, named Mario, who used to know Diane, drops in on the group for some talk and has a surprise of his own.

movies.title: Mon oncle Antoine
movies.overview: Set in cold rural Quebec at Christmas time, we follow the coming of age of a young boy and the life of his family which owns the town's general store and undertaking business.  Mon Oncle Antoine is Director Claude Jutra's masterpiece: A poignant, starkly honest, but humane film, shot through with authenticity from beginning to end.  Realized with an unflagging artistic vision, Mon Oncle Antoine poetically portrays a young boy's coming of age, vividly capturing the Quebec mining town in which he lives.

movies.title: Dirty Money
movies.overview: This French-Canadian crime/action drama, which satirizes U.S. crime films, was shown at the Cannes Film Festival in 1972 and was well received. In the picture, perfectly ordinary people murder, steal, and torture one another with casual abandon in order to solve their everyday problems.

movies.title: Shivers
movies.overview: The residents of a suburban high-rise apartment building are being infected by a strain of parasites that turn them into mindless, sex-crazed fiends out to infect others by the slightest sexual contact.

movies.title: Next of Kin
movies.overview: Twenty-three-year old Peter Foster is an only child who lives at home, where he constantly hears his parents arguing. Because Peter does nothing all day, the family goes to a clinic where a therapist videotapes them. After Peter watches his tape, he views the tape of a troubled Armenian family, who gave their only son away for adoption when they arrived in Canada. Peter decides to visit this family, and he pretends to be their son, Bedros Deryan. The Deryan family welcomes him with open arms, and Peter tries to patch up the poor relationship between George Deryan and his daughter Azah. Written by Will Gilbert

movies.title: I've Heard the Mermaids Singing
movies.overview: Awkward, shy and delightfully funny, Polly Vandersma is an "organizationally impaired" temporary assistant who finally gets her first permanent job at the age of 31. While she works for the curator of an art gallery, Polly narrates her own story, sharing the comical and bittersweet pretensions of the art world. At the same time, she reveals a special part of her own private world, taking the viewer to enchanted places in this quiet assault on the notion of authority everywhere.

movies.title: Tales from the Gimli Hospital
movies.overview: While their mother is dying in the modern Gimli, Manitoba hospital, two young children are told an important tale by their Icelandic grandmother about Ainar the lonely, his friend Gunnar, and the angelic Snjofrieder in a Gimli of old.

movies.title: Speaking Parts
movies.overview: A struggling actor's job as a hotel custodian is a front for his real job: being rented out as a gigolo by his supervisor. A co-worker is obsessed with him, but he ignores and avoids her. He leaves his acting resume in the hotel room of a screenwriter, who is casting for a TV movie based on the true story of her deceased brother. She hires him to play the lead and the two begin an affair. She becomes increasingly distraught as it becomes evident that the movie's producer is changing her story. Egoyan's trademark tangle of bizarre relationships surrounds the protagonists on their way to a mind-blowing conclusion.

content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 1970 to 1989
content_list.description: The Exorcist is released, making audiences around the world sick and causing them to faint, creating a global hysteria. The first blockbuster is released: Jaws; meanwhile, auteur cinema grows with Martin Scorsese and other great directors. The '80s arrive with low-budget productions and era-defining comedies.
